newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell to resume Bonny crude exports at noon.
newsitem.headline: Shell to resume Bonny crude exports at noon.

text.p: The Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group said it would resume the loading of Bonny crude oil from noon on Wednesday after port workers called off a strike.

"The strike is over. The staff of O.I.L. called off the strike at 7.30 (0630 GMT) this morning and we'll resume tanker loading this afternoon around noon," a Shell Nigeria spokesman told Reuters in Lagos.

Staff of the contracting company Ocean Inchcape Limited of Britain, which handles berthing and loading of tankers, began a strike demanding a pay-off because O.I.L had been sold to U.S.-based Tidewater Inc.
"We will lift the force majeure at noon (1100 GMT) so all outstanding nominations will be delayed by three days," the Shell spokesman said.
Bonny crude makes up roughly half of the 950,000 barrels per day (bpd) of the crude oil produced by Shell in Nigeria.

Its oil production is also being threatened in the Warri area in the midwest where there has been tribal fighting over relocation of a local government area but the Shell spokesman said the situation there remained unchanged from the weekend when one flow station was shut down with loss of 2,000 bpd.
